propositions: The outbound comment dedup key is computed from a predicted wire composition in the differ, while the send path independently re-derives the wire through separate compositions; the two compositions have drifted and must be kept in lockstep.
The mutation entry carries only the un-fitted body, but the key predicts the fitted bytes the transport will produce; if the adapter's fit later changes, the key becomes incorrect.

Both mutation-enactment consumers (create path in dispatch_one.py and update path in dispatch_apply_phases.py) must be updated to send the wire_body that was fitted at key-derivation time, not the raw body.

The dedup key must be derived from the actual bytes sent (the readback of wire_body after encoding), not predicted ahead of time, so the differ and send path no longer need to keep separate compositions in sync.
The adapter's defensive fit must remain idempotent: re-fitting an already-fitted body must return it byte-identical, so the key remains sound after the adapter's fit runs again at send time.
Mutation entries written before the cutover (lacking wire_body) must still send, by falling back to the raw body on both enactment paths.
